name: Dark Goldenrod
lede: Dark goldenrod is an X11 web color: a deep, brownish gold that Paterson files among the browns.

sections.title: A web gold
sections.body:
Paterson defines *DarkGoldenrod* as a light brown colour and one of the X11 set, with the hex code #B8860B [1]. In its word lists it sits among the browns [1]. The color is also found in CSS [2]. Its closest named neighbors in our library are [[mustard]] (a CIEDE2000 distance of 9.4) and [[golden-brown]] [2]. It is the darker sibling of [[goldenrod]] [2].

The books say nothing more about this exact shade. The printed phrase is a late arrival: *dark goldenrod* first appears in Google Books around 1960 and peaks in the 1990s [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Dark goldenrod is common as a painted color. It appears in 307 of 23,781 paintings in our archive and is more common than 73% of the named colors [4]. It is mostly an accent (71% of 245 paintings) [4]. It is over-represented in Indian painting, at 3.2 times the expected rate (27 of 721 paintings), and in the Rajput and Pahari schools [4]. George Dawe is its most devoted painter, with 6 of his 50 works here, 5.2 times the baseline [4]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [4].
